clue.text: Gaudy type, this bully

definitions.meaning: a flashy, showy fellow is old slang for a loud dresser
the tormentor of Tom Brown in Tom Brown's Schooldays, later a Victorian anti-hero of novels

explanation.surface: A loud dresser is pointed out as the school tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Brown's Schooldays, a Victorian novel about Rugby School, has a notorious bully who torments the young hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a showy fellow in slang, and the literary schoolboy tyrant of Rugby School.

clue.text: Learned people settled the period, taking half the time

parts.note: a bird that has settled has lit or alighted
an era is a period of history

indicators.note: half the word time is its first two letters

explanation.surface: Scholars settled the dates of an age, using half the allotted time.
explanation.definitionFit: Literati are well-read intellectuals, people of letters.

clue.text: A challenging demand?

parts.note: the insulted gentleman demands redress, a challenge to a duel

explanation.definitionFit: A wronged gentleman once 'demanded' this, meaning amends or a duel.

clue.text: Dance centres may take on Europeans

parts.note: Poles are people from Poland

explanation.surface: Dancing schools may take in students from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Dancers circle the beribboned pole, which is the centre of the May Day dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Garlanded posts that May Day dancers circle with ribbons.

clue.text: Managed to get up lines in the channel

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means the word runs upward, backwards

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it, so ran
rows are lines

explanation.surface: A crew managed to row up the channel.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow strait or channel between two wider bodies of water.

clue.text: The way to divert people?

parts.note: not to amuse them, but the alternative route road traffic is sent along

explanation.definitionFit: A roundabout route that traffic is sent along when a road is closed.

clue.text: Found in pieces of sculpture

definitions.meaning: a statue of head and shoulders

explanation.surface: A statue discovered in fragments.
explanation.definitionFit: Broken in slang; and a carving of head and shoulders.

clue.text: People with a craze to find the total among the strikers

indicators.note: among means set amid the letters of the strikers

parts.note: fists strike blows
to add up is to find the total

explanation.surface: Enthusiasts tally numbers among workers on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Faddists follow passing crazes or fads.

clue.text: Gareth loses head with country nymph

indicators.note: losing its head means the name Gareth drops its opening letter

parts.note: the USA is the usual crossword country of three letters

explanation.surface: A man called Gareth is beheaded alongside a rustic nymph.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she was a nymph changed into a fountain to escape the river god Alpheus.

clue.text: Most etchings include an instruction to the printer

indicators.note: the words Most etchings include the letters spanning their join

explanation.surface: Most etchings carry a note for whoever prints them.
explanation.definitionFit: A proofreader's mark, Latin for 'let it stand', telling a typesetter to ignore a correction.

clue.text: Took off a thousand in desperation, being muddled

indicators.note: being muddled tells us to mix up the letters of the fodder

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Someone fled with a thousand pounds in a panic, all confused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took off' looks like 'ran away' but means mimicked. M and DESPERATION are shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to mimic or imitate them, as an impressionist does.

clue.text: He wants to end something : oil ? no, it's a bit different

indicators.note: a different form of the words means their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone eager to stop a thing is told oil won't do; it's rather different.
explanation.walkthrough: Historically the word named campaigners against slavery.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaigner seeking to abolish a practice, notably slavery.

clue.text: Brave, joining race with 'flu perhaps

parts.note: the human race is mankind, or man

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word flu could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A courageous athlete enters a race despite having influenza.
explanation.definitionFit: Manful means resolute and courageous, as a stout-hearted man is.

clue.text: Commanders have words about Charles's centre

indicators.note: the word words goes about, that is around, the other piece

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the centre of Charles is its middle letters

explanation.surface: Military chiefs argue over a king called Charles.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of Charles, ARL, is put inside WORDS after its W.
explanation.definitionFit: Warlords are military leaders ruling a region by force.

clue.text: Debate finds country breaking records

indicators.note: breaking means the country breaks into the records, splitting them

parts.note: gramophone records are discs
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A discussion reveals a nation smashing sales records.
explanation.definitionFit: To debate a matter is to talk it over or argue it out.

clue.text: Late season to set trap

parts.note: the late someone is dead
fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: The end of the season is the time to set snares.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap in which a heavy weight drops on the prey.

clue.text: Port-Elgar's one diversion

indicators.note: a diversion turns the letters aside onto a new route

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A piece by the composer Elgar offers light entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: ELGARS plus I are rearranged; the possessive 's supplies the S.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Algeria is a major Mediterranean harbour city.

clue.text: Fish the lake in these garments ?

parts.note: ling is a sea fish of the cod family
Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Someone goes fishing in the lake wearing underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Women's underwear and nightclothes.

clue.text: Ida Crane shine in composition ?

indicators.note: composing the letters puts them together in a new order

explanation.surface: Ida Crane glows when composing music.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiance is brightness, a glowing light.

clue.text: People continue doggedly to do it !

definitions.text: People continue doggedly to do it

parts.words: People continue doggedly to do it
parts.note: the clue describes what dogged people do, keep going regardless

explanation.definitionFit: To keep going stubbornly despite obstacles.

clue.text: Medicine for the love-sick? '

parts.note: a remedy against doting, the foolish fondness of a lovesick person; split it as anti plus dote

explanation.definitionFit: A remedy that counteracts poison; read in two halves it is something against doting.

clue.text: Cricketer wanted to get at the beer ?

definitions.meaning: a batsman who starts the innings

definitions.text: wanted to get at the beer
definitions.meaning: a bottle tool needed to prise the cap off

explanation.surface: A thirsty cricketer is eager to reach the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A batsman who begins an innings; and a gadget for uncapping bottles.

clue.text: Point to jolly good posters, perhaps, showing bathing beauties

parts.note: N is a point of the compass, north
A1 means first-rate, written AI in the grid
posters are one kind of advertisement, so ads

explanation.surface: Pointing to fine posters of swimmers on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-class) enters as AI, the digit read as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Naiads were water nymphs of Greek myth dwelling in rivers and springs.

clue.text: Novel is outspoken-sent out to a German

parts.note: frank means candid and outspoken

indicators.note: out signals that the word sent is put out of order

parts.note: ein is German for a

explanation.surface: A book is candidly dispatched to a German reader.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Shelley's gothic book of 1818 about a scientist who builds a creature.

clue.text: Looks composed ?

definitions.meaning: manners or appearances, as in putting on graces

explanation.definitionFit: Affected manners or appearances; and melodies, which are things composed.

clue.text: Where one puts up batting directions ?

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is in
N and S are north and south, two compass directions

explanation.surface: A cricketer asks where to take guard when batting.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'put up' at a place is to stay there overnight, not to raise anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Travellers lodge or stay the night at a hostelry or tavern.

clue.text: Dogs on the pitch?

parts.note: breeds of dog, or, read another way, people who stagger as a ship pitches

explanation.definitionFit: Crossbred hunting dogs; also people who lurch, as passengers do on a pitching deck.
